source.filename: 1990-The deformation of composite beams with discrete flexible connection.pdf

constitutive_assumptions: Shear deformation in solid beam sections is assumed to be very small and is neglected in overall deformation calculations.
Existing analytical closed-form solutions assume continuous (smeared) and linearly elastic connection stiffness along the beam.
Folded plate analysis treats concrete slab segments and steel beam components as elastic plates under three-dimensional elasticity.
The discrete connection interface is modeled as a free-slip boundary with discrete longitudinal reaction forces matched to empirical non-linear push-off load-slip relations.
Plastic section analysis assumes rigid-plastic behavior to compute upper-bound ultimate capacity of partially composite sections.
Standard linear methods assume connection stiffness evaluated as the secant modulus at 50% of the ultimate connector capacity.
control_variables: Simply supported boundary conditions on roller supports.
Four-point loading arrangement with spreader beams across the slab width.
Defined steel beam profiles and profiled metal deck slab configurations across the test matrix.
dependent_variables: Longitudinal slip between concrete slab and steel beam along the span.
Beam secant stiffness at working load relative to theoretical fully composite stiffness.
Shear connector forces and non-linear load-slip behavior.
Ultimate load capacity and ductile failure mode.

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Discrete flexible shear connectors exhibit pronounced non-linear load-slip behavior in push-off tests, influenced by profiling geometry, reduction of concrete confinement in narrow troughs, and discrete separation by steel sheeting.

Four-point bending experiments on composite beams demonstrate that discrete flexible connections result in significant non-linear slip concentrated toward beam ends, leading to additional overall beam deflection.
Standard closed-form and linear continuous connection models underestimate the stiffness of composite beams with partial interaction at working load levels and overestimate maximum end slip.

An extended folded plate method incorporating a free-slip interface and iteratively applied discrete non-linear stud reactions accurately captures three-dimensional beam deformation and the flattening of slip distributions near supports.

Connector stiffness within composite beams subjected to bending appears higher than that determined from pure shear push-off specimens, likely due to friction from support reactions and compressive bending confinement around connector heads.

experimental_setup: Push-off test rigs: standard CP 117 push-off configuration and modified through-deck push-off specimens with profiled metal sheets.
Full-scale simply supported beam testing facility with roller supports and four-point loading via spreader beams.
Deflection and displacement transducers measuring central vertical deflection and longitudinal interfacial slip at discrete intervals along the span.
Eight full-scale composite beams tested with varying spans, decking types, and through-deck welded stud configurations.
future_work: Investigating the mechanisms causing higher connector stiffness in beams relative to push-off tests.
Examining the influence of cross-beam hogging action in the concrete slab over the steel beam.
Conducting push-off tests with larger slab portions and six connectors instead of four.
Testing full-scale composite beams under negative (hogging) moment conditions over the beam.
Assessing the feasibility of reducing the standard code minimum interaction threshold below 50%.
independent_variables: Degree of shear connection / design interaction (ratio of shear connectors relative to full interaction).
Profiled steel decking profile and trough geometry (e.g., standard CP 117, PMF cf 46 with stud at front or rear of trough, Metecno 55, Robertsons QL 60, Holorib).
limitations_inferred: The findings are derived specifically from static four-point bending of civil engineering structural composite beams and cannot be assumed to transfer directly to dynamic, cyclic, or robotic flexural systems without further verification.
The paper does not investigate soft robotic actuators, continuum robots, or miniaturized mechanical devices.
The uncoupled characterization of shear connectors through pure-shear push-off tests fails to capture normal stress and friction interactions present in flexural beam assemblies.
limitations_stated_by_authors: The extended folded plate method requires iterative solution of a large system of simultaneous equations (four times the node count), making it computationally demanding and restricted to large computing platforms.
Individual connector forces could not be directly measured within the full-scale beam tests and could only be approximated by correlating measured slip with separate push-off curves.
The author's method underestimates the maximum end slip despite capturing the flattening of the slip curve near supports.
Existing closed-form analytical methods rely on the assumptions of linear connection stiffness and continuous smearing along the span, which are invalid for discrete flexible connectors.
main_results: Through-deck welded shear studs show significant non-linearity in load-slip response during push-off tests, with reduced stiffness and strength compared to solid slab connectors.
In full-scale beam tests, slip between slab and beam causes marked additional deflection, with slip increasing towards the ends where shear forces are highest.
Beam failure across all eight full-scale tests was ductile, driven by steel yielding in the lower flange following substantial interfacial slip.
Linear and continuous connection models underestimate composite beam secant stiffness at working load levels and overestimate maximum end slip.
The author's non-linear discrete folded plate analysis provides closer agreement with experimental beam stiffness and captures the slip redistribution flattening observed near the beam supports.
Connection stiffness evaluated in full-scale beams is noticeably higher than the secant stiffness measured in isolated push-off tests.
modeling_methods: Folded plate method extended to model discrete non-linear connection with free-slip interfaces and iterative stud reactions.
Plastic section analysis for ultimate flexural capacity.
Engineers' bending theory with modular ratio approach (assuming zero slip).
Empirical linear interaction modification based on degree of interaction (Johnson).
Closed-form second-order differential equations assuming continuous linear elastic connection (Newmark et al.; Johnson).
Finite difference formulation for partial interaction (Roberts).
Finite element analysis with discrete connector elements (Jefferson; Al-Hayderi).
performance_metrics: Interfacial slip along the beam span and end slip (mm).
Secant stiffness at working load as a percentage of theoretical fully composite stiffness (%).
Total load capacity (kN) and distributed load capacity (kN/m²).
possible_gap_implications: Discrete non-linear interface modeling could be explored in layered compliant structures and multi-material beams where continuous bonding assumptions fail to capture localized slip and curvature redistribution.

Pure-shear characterization of flexible connections can underestimate in-situ interfacial stiffness when normal compressive stresses and confinement are present, suggesting the need for coupled interface models in composite flexural systems.
paper.research_objective: To investigate the effect of discrete flexible shear connection and partial interaction on the stiffness, deformation, and load-slip response of composite beams formed with profiled metal decking, and to present and validate a non-linear folded plate analysis method capable of modeling discrete connector behavior.
paper.research_problem: In composite beams designed with partial interaction—particularly those with profiled steel sheeting—discrete flexible shear connectors display non-linear load-slip behavior, causing additional beam deflection and slip that conventional analytical methods (which assume continuous and linear connection) fail to predict accurately.
paper.title: The Deformation of Composite Beams with Discrete Flexible Connection
